question: An electronics retailer's Gemini-based shopping assistant must answer questions such as is this TV in stock at the downtown store and what is today's price, using live data from an inventory API and a pricing service. question: A customer-review platform uses a large Gemini Pro model to extract structured attributes from reviews with 96% accuracy, but at 50 million reviews per month the cost is unsustainable. question: An insurer deployed a custom claims-severity regression model on a Vertex AI endpoint six months ago. Business users report that predictions have become less accurate, but the ML team has no visibility into whether the input data distribution has changed since training. They want automated detection and alerting for such changes using managed features. What should you do?
options: Retrain the model every week regardless of performance to keep it fresh.
Export prediction logs to BigQuery and ask analysts to review histograms monthly.
Replace the regression model with a Gemini prompt that estimates severity.
Enable Vertex AI Model Monitoring on the endpoint to detect training-serving skew and prediction drift for input features, with alert thresholds and notifications.
explanation: Vertex AI Model Monitoring compares the distribution of serving inputs with the training baseline (skew) and with earlier serving windows (drift) for each feature, raising alerts when thresholds are exceeded, which gives the automated visibility the team needs to trigger investigation or retraining. Move the integration to the Gemini API on Vertex AI, which supports IAM, VPC Service Controls, CMEK, regional endpoints and enterprise data governance terms.

question: A telecom operator wants to use Gemini on Vertex AI to summarize customer chat transcripts for agent hand-off. Privacy rules state that names, phone numbers and account identifiers must not be sent to the model or stored in its logs, while summaries must remain useful for agents. Which two design decisions should you include? (Choose two.)
options: Run each transcript through Sensitive Data Protection de-identification (for example, tokenization or replacement of detected PII infoTypes) before sending it to the model, and re-identify only where necessary in the agent UI.
Send the transcript unmodified but instruct the model in the system prompt to omit personal data from the summary.
Disable request-response logging for the Gemini calls and confirm the Vertex AI data governance terms so prompts are not retained for training.
Store the raw transcripts in a public Cloud Storage bucket so the model can retrieve them by URL.
Use the consumer Gemini app to paste transcripts because it is free of charge.
explanation: Sensitive Data Protection detects and de-identifies PII deterministically before data leaves the operator's control, ensuring the model never receives the identifiers while pseudonymous tokens keep the summary coherent, and controlling logging plus relying on Vertex AI's data governance commitments prevents PII from persisting in model-side logs or training data. question: A computer-vision team trains a PyTorch model that currently takes five days on a single 8-GPU VM. options: Submit a Vertex AI custom training job with multiple worker pools of GPU machines using a custom container, enabling Reduction Server to accelerate all-reduce across nodes.
Manually create eight GPU VMs, configure SSH between them, and run torchrun on each host.
Move the training to a single VM with a faster CPU and more memory.
Split the dataset into eight shards and train eight independent models, then average their weights.

question: An autonomous-driving company trains perception models on a GKE cluster with hundreds of GPUs. The training dataset consists of billions of small image files and label files stored in Cloud Storage. GPU utilization is below 40% because data loading is the bottleneck, and the team also needs to write multi-terabyte checkpoints quickly. They want a POSIX-compliant, high-throughput, low-latency file system designed for AI workloads. Which storage option should you recommend?
options: Filestore Basic HDD mounted on every node.
A multi-region Cloud Storage bucket to increase available bandwidth.
A Standard Persistent Disk attached to each node containing a copy of the dataset.
Google Cloud Managed Lustre (or Parallelstore) as a parallel file system, hydrating the dataset from Cloud Storage and using it for checkpoints.
explanation: Managed Lustre and Parallelstore are parallel file systems built for AI and HPC that deliver very high aggregate throughput and sub-millisecond latency for small-file random reads across many clients with POSIX semantics, and they integrate with Cloud Storage for bulk import and export, which eliminates the data-loading bottleneck and supports fast checkpoint writes.
